 1 Task Description
 ELLA is a program for the analysis and evaluation of imposed loads that acts on spatial beam or shell structures in the form of load trains which move along certain traffic lanes. The envelopes of the scalar variables for the entire structure are usually the result. In the case of simple statical systems and simple load cases a traditional analysis of the system can be faster for a large number of imposed load cases under circumstances. The evaluation of influence lines or influence surfaces becomes necessary for an accurate analysis of larger systems, as they are usual particularly in the bridge construction. It is not so simple to determine either the most unfavourable load position or the used parts of a load in order to maximize the certain internal forces for important parts of the structure outside its midspan. In addition, different load positions are critical for the different internal forces and moments. The evaluation of the influence lines reduces the extent of the input very significantly.
 The entire surface of a structure at which imposed loads act gets divided into straight or curved lanes of variable width. Any load trains can be assigned to each lane. They can move indepen- dently or in relation to each other. The traffic lanes are defined with axes which may contain circular segments or clothoids. The loading refers always to the lane axis. An influence line is generated for a vertical loading along the lane’s axis for each lane as well as for a moment loading about the same axis due to the eccentrical parts. Additional influence lines for brake or centrifugal loading can be considered upon request.
 The program evaluates influence lines only for corresponding traffic lanes even in the case of plane structures. However, a satisfactory representation of the two-dimensional effects can be achieved for the available element distribution by partitioning the structure into multiple lanes. The influence surfaces can be either transferred from the database or determined as a rule with a calculation with an own static module of the influence line program.
 In the second case, however, all the single element stiffnesses as well as the stiffness matrix of the entire structure must be available. This requires that at least one load case has been anal- ysed with the programs ASE or STAR2 with option CTRL SOLV 1 or 3, and the corresponding data is still available. Load cases with settlement of support or non-linear load cases are not suitable for this.

Influence lines can be calculated with two completely different methods. The first method deter- mines the deformations (e.g. bending line) due to an unit deformation for the searched internal force (e.g. a break for a moment). The bending area is the result of a static analysis with an appropriate program. A load case defines always one influence area. Corresponding areas are own load cases in each case. This method should be preferred when only a few influence areas or particular variables are to be calculated (e.g. support reactions, deformations or sums of scalar variables).
 When a large number of influence lines of the structure has to be calculated with this method, an own load case will have to be analysed for each cross section and for each internal force. This procedure exceeds usually the available CPU time and memory capacities of the static programs.

The second method works in opposite manner. A unit load is defined at each position (node or member cross section). The analysis determines all the other corresponding internal forces. The main advantage of this method is that the single loads do not have to be applied at every loading location. The missing intermediate values can be calculated easily with an interpola- tion, if the known discontinuities at loading location (break, jump) are considered additionally. Therefore, the number of load cases to be analysed can be reduced significantly.
 In the case of plane structures the discontinuity is defined by means of a singularity. This singularity does not result from a finite element analysis in principal. However we have a smooth approximate influence function which may be used to derive the principal problem of precision in a Finite-Element-Analysis very clearly (see Hartmann/Katz - Structural Analysis with Finite Elements, Springer). This should be considered particularly in the case of shear forces!

At the bottom, bold text reads **“Figure 2.8: Interpolation Grades”**.  

**Overall meaning (as depicted):**  
The graphic contrasts how different interpolation strategies affect the shape of the transverse influence line when interpolating perpendicular to the lane axis in structural analysis. INT 0 represents a case where the influence line remains continuous at the loading location, while INT 1 represents a case where the influence line effect due to eccentricity may contain jumps (typically the most accurate method for plane structures with Mindlin elements, per the contextual text).

When the lane axis does not coincide with the defined nodes, the values of the influence line
 must be interpolated. The program searches then for two series of nodes in the direct vicinity of the lane and interpolates perpendicularly to its axis.
 The selection of a neighboring node series is trivial for plane structures. For girders, however, it is in general a problem for the artificial intelligence. It is extremely difficult for a program to develop the human ability of the general overview. Therefore, this part of the program can not execute in a uniquely determined way. A specific constellation not being recognized correctly can occur again and again. The user must take a proper action in such cases by defining a sequence of nodes or beam elements.
 For the interpolation perpendicularly to the lane axis a distinction must be done very exactly between three variations that result from different types of the load distribution:
 In the first case (INT 0) an eccentrically placed loading generates directly a torsional moment. The influence line of the shear force for the effect of the eccentric influence has no jump in the loading location.
 In the second case (INT 1) the load is replaced by two forces that act at the two girders. The torsional moments result only as a secondary phenomenon due to the constraint of the rotations. The influence line for the effect of the eccentricity may include jumps. This is usually the most accurate method for plane structures analysed with Mindlin elements.
 In the third case (INT 2) torsional moments result additionally from the fixed constraint of the deck slab.
 Following the inverse principle of influence lines it is also possible to view the different meth-
 ods as different interpolation grades of the transverse influence line as shown in the following picture:

The input table defines the parameters of one **SOFiLOAD / ELLA traffic-load lane definition**, where each row item is a configurable attribute controlling lane identity, geometry relative to a given axis, segmentation in the longitudinal direction, and (optionally) deck/track height and cross-fall effects. Each parameter has an associated **unit** and a **default** value or a requirement flag.

## Lane identification and lane type
- **NO (Lane number; `lane_ident.nummer`)**: Integer lane index (default “*” indicates required). Example: `A1.3` means the third lane of axis A1. The special syntax **lane_ident only** means “all/total lanes.”  
- **TYPE (`TYPE`)**: Predefined lane layout literal; value must match recognized standards (also marked “*” = required). These predefined types can trigger automatic creation of secondary lanes based on standard sections.
- **WR (`WR`)**: Right curbstone ordinate, i.e., the coordinate of the right curbstone edge relative to the lane axis. Unit **[m]** with default shown as “-” (no automatic default).
- **WL (`WL`)**: Left curbstone ordinate. Unit **[m]**. Default is **-WR**, meaning the left boundary defaults symmetrically if only WR is given.

## Longitudinal start/end stations and lateral position at stations
The lane can vary along its length by defining coordinates at:
- **SA (`SA`)**: Lane axis coordinate at the **start** (default “!” indicates mandatory).  
- **SE (`SE`)**: Lane axis coordinate at the **end** (default “!” indicates mandatory).

The lane’s lateral placement is defined at start and end by:
- **YCA (Offset of centre at start)**: Unit **[m]**; default `*` (required).
- **YCE (Offset of centre at end)**: Unit **[m]**; default `YCA` (end defaults to start offset if not specified).
- **YRA (Right value at start)**: Unit **[m]**; default `*` (required).
- **YLA (Left value at start)**: Unit **[m]**; default `*` (required).
- **YRE (Right value at end)**: Unit **[m]**; default `YRA` (end right boundary defaults to start right boundary).
- **YLE (Left value at end)**: Unit **[m]**; default `YLA` (end left boundary defaults to start left boundary).

These boundaries control the lane width (left/right edges). The accompanying remarks indicate intersections between lane edges must be handled carefully—only at distinct points—to allow correct treatment of torsional loading.

## Longitudinal segmentation for impact and loaded length dependencies
- **L (`L`)**: Effective length of a segment used for **impact coefficients** and **load-length dependent effects**. Unit **[m]**; default `*` (required).  
  - **CONT**: Special keyword indicating that the current definition continues/extends the previous/last segment; only the first combined definition may specify **L**, while subsequent ones must use `CONT` at that position.

## Vertical parameters (road/rail height and cross fall)
Optional effects related to the elevation and cross-slope of the lane:
- **HSA (`HSA`)**: Height of deck or rail above the lane at **SA**. Unit **[m]**; default **0.0**.
- **HSE (`HSE`)**: Height above the lane at **SE**. Unit **[m]**; default **HSA**.
- **INCA (`INCA`)**: Cross fall at **SA** (in the table shown as `dz/dy` or `Δh [mm]`). Unit **[mm]**; default **0.0**.
- **INCE (`INCE`)**: Cross fall at **SE**. Unit **[mm]**; default **INCA**.

## Railway-specific substructure pressure inputs (rail/bal/track effects)
These parameters support effective pressure calculations below ballast/mountings (as referenced in the provided context):
- **HEFF (`HEFF`)**: Effective height of rail and sleeper. Unit **[m]**; default “-” (typically not auto-filled).
- **BEFF (`BEFF`)**: Effective length of sleeper. Unit **[m]**.
- **DEFF (`DEFF`)**: Effective width of sleeper. Unit **[m]**.
- **INCD (`INCD`)**: Spread angle for stresses. Default **0.25**.
- **ASL (`ASL`)**: Distance between mounting points. Unit **[m]**; default “-”.

## Overall interpretation relative to lane logic (from the remarks)
The remarks explain that **lane 0 must always exist** and that total traffic-load width vs. moving-load width depends on whether additional lanes exist within the curbstone limits. The table parameters above provide the geometry needed to define that axis-referenced lane system, while **L/CONT** enables longitudinal segmentation for load-dependent effects.

### Table description: **LSEL (Lane selection) – parameters controlling lane evaluation**

This table defines the input items for the **LSEL** record, which activates an already defined lane for further evaluation using optional selection of neighboring nodal sequences and load points. A lane can be identified by an axis identifier (4 characters) optionally extended by a “dot + lane number” (e.g., `A1.3`) and may also use wildcards (e.g., `A1.?` or `A1.1?`). If no lane number is given, **all lanes** of the axis are selected, which can increase analysis time.

The table is organized into columns: **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**. Each row specifies a parameter name (left), what it controls (middle), its unit (right), and the default behavior if omitted.

---

#### Core lane and neighbor selection controls

- **NO – Lane identifier**  
  Type `lit8` (lane/ID field). Default is unset (`!`), meaning the user must provide the lane identifier (axis/lane selection target).

- **INT – Load distribution / evaluation mode**  
  Unit: none (`–`). Default: `1`. It controls how load distribution and lane influence evaluation are performed:
  - `0` Single lane  
  - `1` Articulated distribution  
  - `2` Rigid distribution  
  - `3,5,7,9` Trigger *transverse influence line* evaluation based on **QUAD** elements.  
  In combination with the surrounding context, `INT` also influences neighbor-sequence search behavior (how nodes adjacent to the lane are linked into one or two nodal sequences) and whether load points along the axis are subdivided (via `DX` rules). Additionally, a negative `INT` has a special meaning when lanes are defined with **GAX** in the same block: it causes deletion of geometric parameters and influence lines for that lane.

- **DX – Maximum longitudinal distance or direction deviation**  
  Unit: meters (`[m]1001`). Default: `99`. In automatic neighbor linking, `DX` bounds either:
  - spacing of inserted points along the axis (for `INT > 2`), or  
  - the acceptable **angle** between the lane axis and edges of the nodal sequence (for `INT = 0..2`).  
  A negative `DX` permits nodal sequences to intersect the lane (used when intersection angles complicate selection).

- **DY – Influence width of the lane**  
  Unit meters. Default: `99`. Used to define a transverse region to search for neighboring nodes when nodal sequences are not explicitly given. It is measured on both sides of the lane; practical guidance in the text suggests ~90% of the distance between main girders.

- **DZ – Influence height of the lane**  
  Unit meters. Default: `99`. Defines the vertical/examination depth range under the lane axis. For 3D structures, parts above the lane axis are excluded (“Nodes above the lane axis are never considered”). Also governs which QUAD elements qualify during transverse influence evaluation when applicable.

---

#### Explicit node/sequence overrides (manual control)

The table offers two symmetric mechanisms for explicit selection of nodes on the **right-hand side** and **left-hand side** of the lane:

- **RSEL – Explicit centric/right-hand side nodes**  
  Unit: lane node selection expression (`LIT`). Default: `EDGE`.  
  Allowed sub-modes:
  - `EDGE` by nodal sequence `RSEQ`  
  - `SZUG` by continuous beam `RSEQ`  
  - `GRP` by beams of group `RSEQ`  
  - `QGRP` QUADs of group `RSEQ`

- **RSEQ – Selection number for RSEL**  
  No fixed unit (`–`). Default: none (`–`). Provides the identifier referenced by `RSEL` (sequence/beam/group number).

- **LSEL – Explicit left-hand side nodes**  
  Unit: `LIT`. Default: `(RSEL)` meaning it inherits the RSEL selection mode unless separately specified (as reflected in the text’s symmetry of left/right parameters).  
  Same sub-modes as RSEL: `EDGE`, `SZUG`, `GRP`, `QGRP`.

- **LSEQ – Selection number for LSEL**  
  Unitless (`–/Lit` shown). Default: `-`. Identifier referenced by LSEL.

If Ella cannot automatically find suitable neighboring nodal sequences, the table supports manual specification using these explicit selection pathways (including additional sequence selection via boundary/beam definitions in the surrounding text).

---

#### Load train parameters for transverse evaluation only

At the bottom, the table marks items used **only for transverse evaluation** when `INT > 2`:

- **TRAI – Load case of a train for evaluation**  
  Unit `–`. Default: none (`–`). Selects the load train that supplies required wheel-related properties.

- **B – Width of the traffic band (transverse)**  
  Unit meters. Default `*` meaning taken from TRAI unless explicitly overridden.  
  Required for transverse influence line evaluation: must match lane load trains used in lanes to keep longitudinal values consistent.

- **BWH – Distance of wheels (transverse)**  
  Unit meters. Default `*` from TRAI.  
  Differences in wheel spacing are typically only warnings, but correctness is important for consistent load placement.

- **YMAX / YMIN – Eccentricity bounds (overwrite from TRAI)**  
  Units meters. Defaults `+YEX` / `-YEX` respectively, indicating they come from TRAI eccentricity limits unless overwritten explicitly. These bound the minimum/maximum eccentricities used during evaluation.

---

#### Graphical output hook (contextual)
The context also mentions a graphical control option for transverse influence lines via something like `ECHO EL +4`, reinforcing that the `INT=3,5,7,9` modes lead to transverse influence line computations tied to QUAD evaluations.

This table defines the parameter set for **ELLA influence line evaluation** for a specified **scalar variable** (i.e., a force/moment, displacement/rotation, or result-set quantity). Each row lists an input field, what it controls, its unit (often none), and the default behavior.

- **TYPE**: Selects the **scalar variable** for which the influence lines are to be evaluated. It defaults to **LIT**. Conceptually, this chooses the category of result to be computed from the model, covering:
  - beam element forces/moments (e.g., axial **N**, shear **VY/VZ**, torsion/bending moments **MT**, bending components **MY/MZ**, and related),
  - truss/cable/spring quantities (e.g., **TRUS** axial, **CABL** cable force, spring forces/moments like **P**, **PTX/PTY/PTZ**),
  - shell/plate quantities (membrane, shear **VXX/VYY/NXX/NY...**, and bending moments **MXX/MYY/MXY**),
  - nodal displacements/rotations (**UX/UY/UZ**, **PHIX/PHIY/PHIZ**),
  - or defined **result sets** selected via **TYPE RSET:xxxxx** (where `xxxxx` identifies an item within result sets).

- **LMAX**: Specifies the **load case number for the maximum** evaluation. The default is `*`. The table also indicates **0 disables evaluation** for the maximum (i.e., no maximum influence line computation).  
  This field works alongside **LMIN**.

- **LMIN**: Specifies the **load case number for the minimum** evaluation. Also defaults to `*`. Similarly, **0 disables evaluation** for the minimum.

- **FROM**: Defines the **smallest element number** that will be included in the influence line evaluation window. Default is **1**.  
  It is described in the surrounding context as selecting elements for which influence lines are established. If no explicit input occurs for **FROM**, **TO**, and **DELT**, the **entire structure** is selected. It can also accept **group-based selection** (instead of element numbers), e.g. using `FROM 'GRP'` to select an element group.

- **TO**: Defines the **largest element number** included in evaluation. Default is **FROM** (meaning only the range starting at FROM). The context states that **multiple overlapping definitions are possible**, and the **latest positive definition wins**.

- **INC**: Specifies the **increment step** between element numbers when iterating over elements. Default is **1** (evaluate every element in the range). This can reduce workload if set > 1.

- **SYST**: Selects a **subsystem/reduced model context** to evaluate influence lines more efficiently. Default is `*` (full system). It can be set to:
  - **SPAC** or **GIRD** (as stated in context).
  A key optimization rule is given: with **SYST GIRD** (girder-like reduction), certain influence components may be **not calculated/evaluated**, specifically:
  - **axial force** influence lines, and
  - **transverse bending** influence lines.
  This is intended to reduce CPU/memory needs when the imposed loads act on a 2D girder model, even if the global model is 3D due to prestress/temperature.

- **PHI**: Defines an **impact factor or characteristic length** for an impact factor formulation. It has no unit. Default is `*`. The context says: if given with a length unit, PHI corresponds to that length-based characteristic for the impact factor.

Overall, this table configures **what result quantity (TYPE)** is evaluated, **which elements/results are included (FROM/TO/INC/SYST)**, and **which load cases are used for extremal influence lines (LMAX/LMIN)**, with optional **impact-factor scaling (PHI)**.

This table defines up to **six “influence lines” (LINF) that are used along a defined lane axis** for evaluation and output. Influence lines or areas that were stored previously as load cases can be reused for further evaluation. **The results are printed but are not stored in the database**, meaning the table is primarily a configuration for on-demand reporting.

### Columns
- **Item**: Identifier for each configuration field.
- **Description**: Meaning of the field.
- **Unit**: Unit indicator (mostly “–” because the parameters are categorical or refer to load case numbers).
- **Default**: Default value applied if the user does not specify otherwise.

### Influence line definitions (T1…T6 and L1…L6)
For each of up to **six influence line slots**, the table provides:
- **Tn**: *Type* of influence line for slot *n* (n = 1…6).  
  - Default: **MAMI** for each T1–T6.
- **Ln**: *Load case number* that corresponds to the influence line for slot *n* (n = 1…6).  
  - Unit: “–”  
  - Default: “–” (no preset)

Interpretation of **Tn (type)**: The table supports evaluation modes for each influence line:
- **MAMI** = evaluate for **minimum and maximum**
- **MAX** = evaluate for **maximum**
- **MIN** = evaluate for **minimum**
- **ACC** = evaluate only as the corresponding line (i.e., use the influence line “as is” without min/max extraction)

A key behavioral rule: **Positive load case numbers** use the **first set of impact factors (bending)**, while **negative load case numbers** use the **second set (shear)**. Therefore, the sign of each Ln is significant and switches the response category.

### Impact factor / characteristic length (PHI)
- **PHI**: Defines either an **impact factor** or, if a length unit is provided, a **characteristic length used to derive the impact factor**.
- Unit: “–”  
- Default: **“*”** (unspecified in the table, meaning it depends on system context or calculation settings)

### Title (TITL)
- **TITL**: **Title of the influence line** configuration/output.
- Default: **“*”** (context-dependent)

### Overall purpose
This configuration table allows the user to select and parameterize **up to six pre-stored influence lines** by:
1) specifying each influence line’s **type of evaluation** (T1–T6),
2) assigning the related **load case numbers** (L1–L6) with sign controlling **bending vs shear**,
3) optionally setting an overall **impact factor/characteristic length** via **PHI**,
4) labeling the output with **TITL**.

See also: CalculationofInfluenceAreas, LANE, ECHO, SHOW
 LINF
 Influence lines or areas which were stored as load cases can be taken over for the evaluation along the defined lane axis. However, results are only printed and do not get stored in the database.
 Up to six corresponding influence lines can be defined together.
 For type T1 to T6 one can enter:
 MAMI = Evaluation for minimum and maximum
 MAX = Evaluation for maximum
 MIN = Evaluation for minimum
 ACC = Evaluation only as corresponding line
 Positive load case numbers are processed with the first set of impact factors (bending), while negative load case numbers use the second set (shear).

The table describes input parameters used for calculating influence lines and additional loading locations within a beam model (cross sections along an element). It contains four columns: **Item** (parameter name), **Description** (meaning and valid values), **Unit** (measurement/notation), and **Default** (system default if the user does not specify the parameter).

### Parameters

**1) TYPE**  
- **Purpose:** Defines the **direction/content of the unit forces** used in the influence line calculation.  
- **Unit/format:** Listed as **LIT** (internal notation/flag rather than a physical unit).  
- **Default:** **STAN**.  
- **Allowed values and interpretation:**
  - **MONO** – “Only centric vertical loading” (unit forces applied only as vertical, centered/canonical loading).
  - **STAN** – “Only vertical loading” (vertical unit forces without additional traversal/longitudinal effects). This is also the default.
  - **TRAV** – “Additionally traverse loading” (extends the loading pattern to include traversing effects; described in the context text as useful primarily for **three-dimensional systems** with corresponding loads).
  - **FULL** – “Additionally longitudinal loading” (extends the loading pattern to include longitudinal effects; also indicated as relevant mainly for **three-dimensional systems**).

**2) TGEN**  
- **Purpose:** Controls the **accuracy of cross-section jumps** for the placement of additional loading locations within a beam element. It determines the threshold for inserting extra locations based on how rapidly the reciprocal stiffness changes along neighboring cross sections.  
- **Unit:** “–” (dimensionless / parameter-like).  
- **Default:** **0.**  
- **Contextual rule (from the accompanying text):** A **loading location is inserted** when the **difference of the reciprocal stiffness** between two neighboring cross sections is larger than a multiple of **TGEN**. In other words, TGEN acts as a sensitivity/threshold parameter: larger values generally reduce the number of inserted locations by demanding a larger stiffness jump before adding a new location.

### Behavioral/Performance Context
The provided context also notes that CPU time for obtaining influence lines can be reduced by using the **default value of APPL**, and that **TRAV** and **FULL** options are only beneficial for specific **3D loading cases**. Additionally, **TGEN** defines at which positions along the beam element the additional loading locations are generated, based on the stiffness-change criterion described above.

The input table defines parameters for generating a plotted “paper” (output sheet) and for controlling which structural influence/load graphics are drawn, including their visual styling via “pen numbers”.

**TYPE (paper size)**: Controls page orientation. A positive value selects *landscape* format; a negative value selects *portrait* format. Unit is dimensionless (“–”). Default is **-lp** (implying portrait by default unless overridden).

**SC (scale)**: Global scaling factor for the output. Unit is “–”. Default is **\*** (meaning a system or program-dependent default scale).

**W (paper width)** and **H (paper height)**: Physical dimensions of the sheet. Both are measured in **cm** and default to “–” (i.e., use whatever default paper size is implied by TYPE/SC or configuration).

**MARG (border drawing configuration)**: Determines whether and how a border is drawn around the sheet. Unit is **LIT** (enumeration). Options:
- **OFF**: no border  
- **NO**: only an inner border  
- **YES**: adds an additional outer border  
- **FULL**: draws an additional border around the sheet (full framing)  
Default is **FULL**.

**FORM (form of the border)**: Selects the border/frame style type (again an enumerated value in **LIT**):
- **STAN**: standard frame  
- **ZTVK-88**: ZTVK-88 frame variant  
- **URS**: URSULA definition  
Default is **ZTVK**.

**HDIV (number of the representations per sheet)**: Controls how many representations/graphic partitions are placed on a single sheet. Unit is “–”. Default is **\***.

**C1–C9 (pen numbers and fill area selection)**: These items define which “pen” is used for specific categories of lines and areas; pen numbers control line appearance and whether they are plotted.
- **C1**: pen for *vertical influence lines* (default **1000**)  
- **C2**: pen for *torsional influence lines* (default **1001**)  
- **C3**: pen for *transverse influence lines* (default **1002**)  
- **C4**: pen for *longitudinal influence lines* (default **1003**)  
- **C5**: pen for *positive uniform loadings* (default **0**)  
- **C6**: pen for *negative uniform loadings* (default **0**)  
- **C7**: reserved pen number (default **-** unspecified)  
- **C8**: pen for *loadings* (default **2001**)  
- **C9**: *fill area number* for loadings (default **2235**)

**Additional rendering context from the provided notes**: Graphical representations are produced only when the record **SIZE** is provided. If a pen number is defined *negatively*, the corresponding line type will **not** be plotted. Line plotting is controlled by the **SHOW** record: the set of lines to be plotted is prescribed with SHOW. If **ECHO** is used, the load position (**LPOS**) is visualized in addition to influence lines; without **ECHO**, only influence lines are shown. Also, the item mentioned (SIZE context) subdivides the sheet into strips so multiple influence lines can be drawn in the same drawing area: positive values subdivide with alignment along paper width and subdivision in height; negative values invert this behavior. The default stated for this subdivision is “three lines” plotted parallel to the largest dimension of the paper.

This table defines the parameter options for a record controlling the selection and presentation of **influence lines** (context: “SHOW … lines which should be printed (record ECHO IL) and / or plotted (record SIZE) are selected”). The table is organized by **Item** (parameter name), **Description** (what the parameter does and valid keyword values), **Unit** (mostly “–”, i.e., dimensionless or context-dependent), and **Default** (default value if the item is not specified).

### Parameters and meanings

- **SNO (Lane number)**  
  Selects which “lane” (i.e., a predefined numbering/placement concept) of influence lines is handled.  
  - Default: **0**

    - **0** = all (implied by “0 all”)  
    - **lit4** = “all lanes of axis ’lit4’”

The input table defines the structure and semantics of an “action” record in a load-combination system (e.g., SOFiLOAD/MAXIMA context). Each row specifies an item/field name, a human description of what the field controls, the expected unit (mostly dimensionless), and a default behavior indicating whether a value is prefilled (via design-code INI defaults).

**1) TYPE (Designation of action)**  
- **Meaning:** A code identifying the action type (with defaults shown as “LIT4” in the table example).  
- **Role:** Selects the action definition preset (and determines valid combinations and default coefficients).  
- **Default column:** “!” indicates a required field or non-optional behavior (in the table’s convention).

**2) Partial safety factors and combination coefficients (GAMU, GAMF, PSI0–PSI2, PS1S, GAMA)**  
These fields are scalar coefficients (unit “–”) used in ultimate/serviceability combination rules:
- **GAMU:** *Unfavourable partial safety factor* (dimensionless).  
- **GAMF:** *Favourable partial safety factor* (dimensionless).  
- **PSI0:** *Combination coefficient rare*  
- **PSI1:** *Combination coefficient frequent*  
- **PSI2:** *Combination coefficient quasi-permanent*  
- **PS1S:** *Combination coefficient infrequent*  
- **GAMA:** *Partial safety factor accidental*  
All are shown with “*” in the default column, meaning they typically come from the design-code INI defaults unless explicitly overwritten.

**3) PART (Partition / classification into action groups)**  
- **Meaning:** Assigns the action to the temporal variance group used by superposition equations.  
- **Listed options:**  
  - **G:** permanent action (e.g., dead load)  
  - **P:** prestress  
  - **Q:** variable action  
  - **Q_1 … Q_99:** variable action load groups (for combination strategies that avoid intermediate superpositions and enable staged MAXIMA processing)  
  - **A:** accidental action  
  - **E:** seismic action  
- **Default:** “*” indicates code-dependent defaults; also, the accompanying text stresses a key rule: for user-defined actions, **PART must be given** to keep categories consistent (all categories of the same action share the same PART; only the Q-group number may differ).

**4) SUP (Default superposition rule within the action)**  
- **Meaning:** How multiple load cases/categories inside the same action are combined or excluded under defaults.  
- **Default column:** “*” (INI-defined unless overridden).  
- **Supported modes (as listed):**  
  - **PERM:** permanent with unique factor (sum decisive; favourable/unfavourable applied to the total depending on convention)  
  - **PERC:** permanent with individual factors (load-case-wise favourable/unfavourable)  
  - **COND:** conditional (take decisive load cases depending on unfavourability)  
  - **EXCL:** mutually exclusive within category  
  - **EXEX:** mutually exclusive within the action (stronger exclusion; only the worst-case from the action side is considered)  
  - **UNSI:** COND with unfavourable sign  
  - **USEX:** EXCL with unfavourable sign  
  - **ALEX:** permanent but exclusive within action (only one load case per action considered for superposition, even if favourable)  
The text further notes that for “leading Q” or “leading G” action types, SUP defaults change (EXCL → COND for Q-type, etc.), but free overrides are possible per load case.

**5) TITLE (Designation/label of action)**  
- **Meaning:** Human-readable name for the action record.  
- **Default:** “*” indicates a non-mandatory or optional default label behavior.

**Overall table intent:**  
The record collectively specifies (a) what the action *is* (TYPE/TITLE), (b) what numeric factors apply (GAMU/GAMF/PSI*/GAMA), (c) where it belongs in the time-variance superposition framework (PART, including load-group partitioning), and (d) how its internal load cases are treated with respect to conditionals and mutual exclusions (SUP). The surrounding context emphasizes that these defaults are driven by the selected design-code INI-files and may need redefinition when the design code changes, and that action categories inherit PART but can still differ via load-group indexing (Q_1…Q_99) and SUP-driven inclusion/exclusion behavior.

The input table is a compact mapping between **SOFiLOAD action superposition settings** (column “SOFiLOAD”) and their corresponding **MAXIMA load-case combination treatment** (column “MAXIMA”), plus a short semantic explanation (column “Explanation”). It primarily classifies how multiple load cases belonging to an action (and/or categories within the action) are combined in MAXIMA.

**Columns:**
- **SOFiLOAD**: the literal keyword used in SOFiLOAD to define the default superposition rule for an action (or category group).
- **MAXIMA**: the corresponding internal MAXIMA “LC TYPE” token or record type used to implement that rule (e.g., `PERM`, `COND,Q`, `An0`, `AGno`), sometimes with symbolic placeholders (`n`, `no`).
- **Explanation**: human-readable meaning, describing selection/exclusion and whether factors are applied “always” or only in an “unfavourable” case.

**Rows (semantic rules):**
1. **PERM → PERM,G**: “always (permanent), partial safety factor action-wise”. All permanent load cases of the action are included; the safety factor application is effectively **action-level** rather than load-case-wise.
2. **PERC → PERC**: “always (permanent) with variable factors, partial safety factor load-case-wise”. Permanent loads are still always included, but partial safety factors can differ **per load case**.
3. **COND → COND,Q**: “conditional (only unfavourable)”. The action’s contributions are used only if they lead to an unfavourable effect.
4. **EXCL → Ano**: “mutually exclusive. MAXIMA record LC different alternative group numbers per category”. Within the action, mutually exclusive categories/alternatives are handled such that only one alternative group/category choice is used at a time; the `n` indicates grouping via MAXIMA alternative group identifiers.
5. **EXFEX → Ano**: “mutually exclusive but conditional inclusive categories (only within an action)”. As with exclusion, but with an additional conditional-inclusive behavior: alternative group selection is applied such that only one alternative group number is used for the action’s categories (implemented through a single alternative group id in MAXIMA).
6. **UNSI → W**: “changing sign (e.g. seismic actions)”. Used for actions whose effect may reverse; MAXIMA treats them with a sign-changing mode.
7. **USEX → Xno**: “changing sign, mutually exclusive within input of an alternative group number in MAXIMA record LC”. Combines sign-changing behavior with mutual exclusivity controlled by MAXIMA alternative group numbering.
8. **ALEX → AGno**: “always but exclusive (only within an action) with input of an alternative group number in MAXIMA record LC”. Only one load case/category representative is considered within the action, but—unlike purely conditional modes—it is treated as **always** eligible; `AGno` ties to the alternative group id.

**RAG relevance / how to use the table:** This mapping is essential for interpreting how an **SOFiLOAD action type** drives MAXIMA’s **superposition/combination logic**, especially for “always vs conditional”, “mutual exclusivity”, “sign-changing” actions, and the role of **alternative group numbers** in MAXIMA records. The placeholders (`n`, `no`) indicate that multiple distinct alternative groups are supported by numeric identifiers.

It specifies the input fields (“Item”), their meanings (“Description”), the expected units (“Unit”), and system defaults (“Default”). The record is centrally used to control not only the selection/type of loading train but also spatial placement (lane position and eccentricity), repetition (convoy distance), and load multiplicative factors and impact effects.

- **TYPE**: Selects the **type of load train** (column “Type of a load train”). The table shows the default as **CONs** and the unit/type token as **LIT**, indicating a categorical selector. The provided context lists many available standards (e.g., **LM71, UIC71, SW/0, SW/2, railway fatigue RFAT, EC HSLM, BS5400 RL**, etc.).
- **P1–P4**: Provide up to four numerical values used by the chosen **TYPE**. They are generic placeholders for load parameters that different train definitions interpret differently. Units are **kN, m** and defaults are shown as **\*** (meaning no fixed default; depends on TYPE).

### Area and environmental loading components
- **P5 (kN/m²)**: “Loading on spare areas.” Context clarifies it is applied **without dynamic impact factors and without centrifugal forces**, and only for certain lane/geometry regions (residual areas between train constant width and lane polygon bounds, between lane 0 and other lanes, and total lane area for group **GR4**, such as pedestrian bridges). If train width **WIDT = 0**, residual area is not produced (noted for railways).
- **P6**: “Wind loading” (unit **\***), and **P7** gives geometry/height of the wind attack area or the wind load application height (unit **[m]1001**).
  - Context notes optional modelling: traffic-band area load **P6** over height **P7** for horizontal wind; AASHTO alternative uses a line load at height **P7**.
- **P8**: “Parameter for brake load” with type-dependent meaning; its sign/direction follows moving direction unless controlled by **DIR B** logic in the wider system (context mentions ELLA/SOFILOAD handling direction changes or deactivation).
- **P9**: “Height of mass center (centrifugal load and cross fall)” (unit **[m]1001**), used when centrifugal/crossfall-related effects are enabled.

### Factors and geometric placement
- **PFAC**: Multiplier applied to **all load elements of the load train**; default shown as **1.0**.
- **PFAV**: Multiplier for “favorable effects within load trains” (wheel-load-only for road trains); default is **\*** (context describes specific defaults like railway LM71: 0.0 and others: 1.0; many road trains default to 0.0 unless overridden per individual train definition).
- **WIDT**: Train **width** (unit **[m]1001**). This width governs residual-area loading behaviour for **P5**.

### Impact and motion-dependent parameters
- **PHI**: Explicit **impact factor for bending** (default \*).
- **PHIS**: Explicit **impact factor for shear** (default \*).
- **V**: “Speed of load train” (unit **[km/h]1203**, default \*). Used for dynamic/impact-related effects in many load formulations.
- **FUGA**: “Factor for the masses of total train for the centrifugal forces” (unit –, default **1.0**). Appears specifically for multi-body/dynamic centrifugal scaling.

### Convoy repetition, eccentricity, and direction controls
- **XCON (m)**: Minimum distance for repeated load trains (convoy). Default **0** meaning no repetition beyond the base definition. Context explains the train can be applied multiple times with that distance between the last load ordinate and the reference point of the next train.
- **YEX (m)**: Possible eccentricity of train **(+/-)**. Default **0.0**. Context elaborates: for railway loadings default eccentricity is based on **±r/18** and creates additional moments; for road loadings it provides a total offset to left/right.
- **DIR**: “Direction of train” with categorical values:
  - **B** = both directions,
  - **R** = only to the right (positive),
  - **L** = only to the left (negative),
  - **N** = do not apply.
  Context notes that **DIR** controls generation sequence and braking/load sign conventions; if **DIR N** is specified, impact is suppressed and brake/velocity/wind preset to zero.
- **DIRT**: “Direction of transverse loading” similarly with values **B/R/L/N** to control suppression or sign of transverse/wind/transverse-direction loading; context notes direction handling and combined logic with other options.

- **Residual area loading P5 (special static rule)**: The “residual area loading P5” is applied **without dynamic impact factors and without centrifugal forces**, and only under limited geometric conditions:
  - between constant-width load train edges and the **polygonal bounds of the lane**,
  - between **lane 0 borders** and other lanes (e.g., pathways),
  - and the **total lane area** for load group **GR4** (e.g., pedestrian bridges).
  - If the load train has **no width (WIDT = 0)**, then no residual area is applied (noted for railways).

  - railway: default **0.0 for LM71**, **1.0 for other railway trains**,
  - most other road trains: default **0.0**.
  - These factors may only be specified with **individual load train definitions** for roads.

  - The eccentricity within the lane should generally be defined **only when applying the loading**.
  - Only for **wide heavy load trains** (LM3, HB, etc.) may eccentricity be defined in advance.
  - For railway, YEX is intended to match **EN 1991-2 6.3.5**, with a predefined default of **± r/18** in both directions.
  - For railway loadings, additional moments are generated; for road loadings, the train gets an **overall lateral offset** (default 0.0).

  - Load trains have a **moving direction** that affects braking-load direction and braking sequence effects.
  - **Positive** load values are braking loads **in the traveling direction**, **negative** values are accelerating loads in reverse.
  - If **DIR N** is specified: **no impact factor** is applied and braking, velocity, and wind preset to zero; some filters in “ELL A” apply.
  - **DIR** controls the sequence for a **standard** train but cannot reverse sequences for **user-defined** trains.

  - Defined via a wind **attack area** with a section definition.
  - With combined wind+traffic, a horizontal area load **P6** can act on a traffic band of height **P7**; AASHTO instead uses a line load P6 at height P7.

- **Meaning of P8**:
  - P8 is interpreted differently by load type.
  - Braking sign comes from moving direction; a changing sign via **DIR B** may be handled by ELLA. ELLA/SOFILOAD can change direction or deactivate loading; options combine with logical AND.

  This value is the **total weight parameter** associated with the selected HS/HL-93 train.

    - **P1=15 → (19.5/13.5) kip**

    - **P1=15 → 0.48 klf**
    - **P1=20 → 0.64 klf**
  - HL-93:
    - **US → 0.64 klf**

It is organized into three main groups: **(1) global force components and positional/influence parameters**, **(2) wheel/area discretization geometry parameters**, and **(3) optional multi-body dynamics (animation and spring–damper) parameters**.

### 1) Core load components, heights, and influence-region parameters
Each row specifies an **Item**, a textual **Description**, an **Unit**, and a **Default**.

- **P**: vertical load magnitude. Unit **[kN]₁₁₉₀**; default **0.0**. This is the main axle/wheel vertical component.
- **PB**: longitudinal component for braking/accelerating. Positive means **braking** in travelling direction; negative indicates **acceleration** opposite direction. Unit **[kN]₁₁₉₀**; default **0.0**.
- **PW**: transverse load component (e.g., bumping, wind). Unit **[kN]₁₁₉₀**; default **0.0**.
- **PF**: vertical load value used specifically for **centrifugal** loading. Unit **[kN]₁₁₉₀**; default **P** (i.e., same as vertical load unless overridden).
- **PFAC**: factor for favourable components; Unit **—**; default **0.0** (indicates a modification/scaling behaviour governed by “remarks/OPT” context).
- **DIST**: minimum/absolute distance parameter controlling spacing between loads in the train: “A is Minimum (MIN) / absolute (ABS) distance” with reference to **LIT**. Unit **[m]₁₀₀₁**; default **ABS**.
- **A**: distance to the last load of the train (spacing definition between successive load points). Unit **[m]₁₀₀₁**; default **0.0**.
- **DPOS**: minimum distance to the load reference point (point). Unit **[m]₁₀₀₁**; default **0.0**.
- **DMIN** / **DMAX**: influence region extents **before** and **behind** the load; Unit **[m]₁₀₀₁**; both default **0.0**.
- **Y**: eccentricity to the lane axis, with **sign convention**: “> 0 = to the right”. Unit **[m]₁₀₀₁**; default **0.0**.
- **HW**: total height of wind attack area (for transverse/impact-related effects). Unit **[m]₁₀₀₁**; default **0.0**.
- **ZW**: height of the horizontal force. Unit **[m]₁₀₀₁**; default **HW/2** (implies a centre-of-pressure assumption).
- **HF**: height of mass center (used in dynamic/centrifugal or multi-body formulations). Unit **[m]₁₀₀₁**; default **0.0**.
- **PHI**: impact and special options bit/flag set controlling several behaviours (see remarks). Unit **—**; default **1**.

### 2) Wheel discretization and contact-area parameters
These items control how the load is distributed across wheels/axle and along wheel contact length:

- **NW**: number of wheels on an axle; stated range **(0–7)**. Default shown as **\*** (not fixed in this table; likely depends on other settings/required input when used).
- **B**: distance of wheels across the lane (transverse spacing). Unit **[m]₁₀₀₁**; default **0.0**.
- **BW**: width of wheel contact area. Unit **[m]₁₀₀₁**; default **0.0**.
- **LW**: length of wheel contact area. Unit **[m]₁₀₀₁**; default **0.0**.

Interpretation notes from the provided context: if **NW = 0**, vertical load values are converted into a **distributed load over the train width (WIDT)** and clipped to the current lane width. Otherwise, loads can be treated as a **single point load**, a **pair of wheels** (when **B < WIDT**), or a **distributed load/area loading** depending on **BW** and whether **B equals WIDT**. The remarks also clarify that **ELLА uses only resultant forces** for influence-line evaluation (wheel contact true dimensions mainly matter for copy/export in SOFiLOAD).

### 3) Multi-body dynamics / animation parameters (optional)
The lower section introduces parameters for generating a structural dynamic representation of the vehicle/load train via record **TREX** (and related structural association), including frequencies and modal damping:

- **SNO**: section number for animation. Unit **—**; default **—**.
- **FRB**: frequency for body spring. Unit **1/sec**; default **\***.
- **DAB**: modal damping of body support. Unit **—**; default **\***.
- **BOGI**: load value of bogie. Unit **—/kN** (sign indicates formulation convention); default **\***.
- **FRBO**: frequency for bogie spring. Unit **1/sec**; default **\***.
- **DABO**: modal damping of bogie support. Unit **—**; default **\***.
- **WHEE**: load value of wheel. Unit **—/kN**; default **\***.
- **FRWH**: frequency for wheel spring. Unit **1/sec**; default **\***.
- **DAWH**: modal damping of wheel support. Unit **—**; default **\***.

Overall, the table serves as a compact specification for describing how much load (vertical, longitudinal, transverse), where it acts (position through A/DPOS, lane eccentricity Y, and optional influence region MIN/MAX), and how it is discretized across wheels/areas (NW/B/BW/LW) are to be applied—optionally extended with dynamics/animation parameters for multi-body simulations.

The table defines the **parameter inputs for TRBL** (freely defined **vertical/transverse line load trains** with additional options), which are used in the context of multi-body dynamics records (referenced to **TREX**). It also connects conceptually to other records (TRAI, TRPL, LANE, TREX, and TRBL itself), where TRPL provides general remarks for load trains and the current table supplies the detailed quantities needed to construct the load geometry and optional dynamic components.

### Core load components (general)
- **P** *(kN/m)*: vertical load value (default **0.0**).
- **PB** *(kN/m)*: braking load value (default **0.0**).
- **PW** *(kN/m)*: load value in the transverse direction (default **0.0**).
- **PF** *(kN/m)*: vertical load value specifically for centrifugal loading; default equals **P** (i.e., inherits vertical load).
- **PFA C** *(–)*: factor for favourable components (default **0.0**). Used to scale/suppress favourable contributions.

### Load-length control and spatial extent
- **DIST**: defines whether position/length data is treated as **Minimum (MIN)** or **absolute (ABS)**; option shown as **LIT**, with default **ABS**.
- **A** *(m)*: distance to the **last** load of the train (default **0.0**).
- **L** *(m)*: fixed or minimum load length. Can be positive or negative; **0 = unlimited** (default **0.0**).
- **LMAX** *(m)*: maximum length of the load train (unit m; default not shown as explicit value in the table).
- **LDEL** *(m)*: discrete variable length defined as **L + n·LDEL** (default **0.0**).

### Geometry: eccentricity and wind-related heights
- **Y** *(m)*: eccentricity to the lane axis (**>0 to the right**) (default **0.0**).
- **HW** *(m)*: total height of the wind attack area (default **0.0**).
- **ZW** *(m)*: height of resulting force **PW**; default **HW/2**.
- **HE** *(m)*: height of the mass centre (default **0.0**).

### Impact and special options
- **PHI** *(–)*: impact and special options controlling interpretation/behaviour (remarks referenced in text). Default **1**.

### Track distribution parameters (line vs. distributed loads)
- **NW** *(–)*: number of tracks on an axle (**0–2**). Default marked with **\*** (unspecified/variable).
- **B** *(m)*: distance of tracks across the lane (default **0.0**).
- **BW** *(m)*: width of track contact area (default **0.0**).

These variables govern how loads are “spread” across lane width:
- If **NW = 0**, the load train values are converted from line loads into **distributed loads over lane width** using **WIDT**, and then **clipped** at the lane boundary.
- If **NW > 0**, one or more **line loads** are created at track positions using **B**; if **BW** is provided, an **area load** can be created instead of a line load.

### Optional animation / multi-body dynamics parameters
- **SNO** *(–)*: section number for animation (no default specified).
- Multi-body dynamics parameters are included but, per the provided context:  
  **“Input values for multi-body-dynamics of line loads TRBL for record TREX will not be used currently.”**
  Therefore, the following entries are structurally present but may be inactive in practice:
  - **FRB** *(1/sec)*: frequency for body spring **Cb**.
  - **DAB** *(–)*: modal damping of body support.
  - **BOGI** *(–/kN)*: load value of bogie.
  - **FRBO** *(1/sec)*: frequency for bogie spring **Cbo**.
  - **DABO** *(–)*: modal damping of bogie support.
  - **WHEE** *(–/kN)*: load value of wheel.
  - **FRWH** *(1/sec)*: frequency for wheel spring **Cwh**.
  - **DAWH** *(–)*: modal damping of wheel support.

Overall, the table primarily specifies how to construct a **spatially positioned load train** (magnitudes P/PB/PW/PF, eccentricity, length/discretization, and lane/track distribution), with additional optional dynamic parameters that are currently stated to be ignored when used with TREX.

The input table contains two configuration fields related to how eccentricity and load-train positioning are handled during an evaluation case. It is intended to control the algorithmic selection of the most unfavorable loading arrangement within a predefined lane (context: lanes define where the load train may act; loadings outside lane width are ignored). The record CASE is assumed to be followed by corresponding POSL (positioning superposition load) records; however, this table specifically documents sub-options for the lane-eccentricity and the selection strategy for load-train placement on the influence line.

### Columns
- **Item**: Short identifier of the parameter (e.g., EXCE, EXTR).
- **Description**: Human-readable meaning and the allowed symbolic values with behavior implications.
- **Unit**: Declared unit/type for the parameter. In both cases it is shown as **LIT**, indicating a literal/enumerated choice rather than a numerical physical unit.
- **Default**: Default activation/behavior when the parameter is not explicitly set.

### Parameters

#### 1) EXCE — Automatic selection of eccentricity
- **Meaning**: Controls whether the evaluation program should automatically determine the eccentricity (transverse offset) of the applied loading within the lane limits, or whether this automatic selection is disabled.
- **Enumerated values**:
  - **AUTO**: *Automatic selection activated*. The program will choose an eccentricity considered most unfavorable within the allowed eccentric range.
  - **FIX**: *Automatic selection deactivated*. Eccentricity is treated as fixed (implying that a predetermined eccentric value is used rather than searching).
- **Default**: **FIX**  
  This means that, unless EXCE is set to AUTO, eccentricity auto-optimization will not be performed.

#### 2) EXTR — Selection of load train position
- **Meaning**: Determines the criterion used to select the extreme (most unfavorable) position of the load train along the lane/influence line search process. This affects how the program decides which placement yields the maximum relevant response.
- **Enumerated values**:
  - **VERT**: Extremes are selected **according to vertical loading**.
    - The algorithm emphasizes response contributions driven by vertical loads when evaluating the influence of different load-train positions.
  - **ALL**: Extremes are selected **according to all load components**.
    - The program considers the combined effect of the full loading set (e.g., vertical and other components) when identifying the extreme position.
- **Default**: **ALL**  
  By default, the algorithm searches for the most unfavorable position considering the full set of load components, consistent with the overall goal of maximizing forces (as described in the context).

### Overall interpretation in the lane evaluation workflow
Together, **EXCE** and **EXTR** steer the extremum search:
- **EXCE** governs whether eccentricity within the lane is auto-optimized to produce an unfavorable torsional/side position.
- **EXTR** governs whether the load train’s longitudinal position extremes are derived solely from vertical effects or from the entire loading vector.

The input table defines the parameters for a **COMB (combination) record** used to create a superposition of multiple *evaluation cases* for structural load analysis. It documents the meaning of the **row/field items**, their **descriptions**, the **expected unit**, and any **default values**.

## Overall purpose
A COMB record describes how to combine several evaluation cases into one intermediate result. The rule determines which cases are mutually exclusive (by default) and, in special situations, enables **superposition and variant superposition conditions** where partial results are combined according to factors.

## Field: TYPE (Unit: LIT, Default: Q)
The first section specifies **TYPE**, which selects the superposition type/grouping logic used for the combination:
- **G**: permanently acting
- **Q**: acting only if unfavourable
- **A0…A9**: alternative groups (alternative group 0 through 9)
- **F**: additional evaluation case to add

This field effectively controls the combination semantics. For example, alternative groups are later used to select the “most unfavourable” among cases in that group according to the assigned superposition rule.

## Fields for load selection and scaling: L1/F1 … L10/F10
The next part lists repeated parameters for up to **ten** evaluation cases within one COMB definition:
- **L1**: number or range of evaluation case(s) for the first load component
- **F1**: factor applied to those evaluation case(s) (Default for factors: **1.0**)
- **L2**, **F2**
- **L3**, **F3**
- …
- **L10**, **F10**

### Interpretation of “L” fields
Each **Lx** is either:
- a single evaluation case number (e.g., `2`), or
- a case number range (e.g., `2:9`)

These ranges are used for internal selection rules where only cases without already-loaded lanes are considered, enabling combining multiple track/lane scenarios.

### Interpretation of “Fx” fields
Each **Fx** is a scalar multiplier applied to the selected evaluation case(s). If not specified, the default factor is **1.0** (as shown in the table). The factors allow weighted selection among ordered unfavourability cases, e.g., most unfavourable at 1.0, second most at 0.6, etc.

## Constraints and extension mechanism (implied by table context)
The table shows only **L1…L10** (max ten components), but the surrounding context clarifies that if more than ten cases must be combined, additional COMB records with **TYPE = F** (“additional evaluation case to add”) can be used to extend the combination.

## RAG indexing takeaway
Store this table as defining the COMB parameter schema:
- **TYPE** defines superposition/selection mode (G, Q, A0–A9, F).
- **L1…L10** identify evaluation case numbers or ranges.
- **F1…F10** provide scaling factors (default 1.0).
These fields together specify how COMB selects and weights evaluation cases to form intermediate combined results.

This input table describes **station-by-station information for a single lane** as part of a road/track geometry and influence-line output. It is intended to support geometry reconstruction and subsequent calculations related to lane behavior (e.g., spacing, alignment progression, and position-dependent properties).

### Table purpose and scope
The table provides a **sequence of stations** along the lane and lists, for each station, the **key spatial coordinates** and the **advance step** to the next station. In the broader output context, lane geometry can be controlled using **ECHO LINE**. The default output produces a **separate table per lane**, whose headline includes lane influence parameters (e.g., **DY influence width**, **DZ influence height**, and **Load distribution** reference, see record **LSEL**). This station table complements those headline parameters by giving the geometric sampling along the lane.

With **ECHO LINE FULL**, the system additionally reports **neighboring nodes** on the **left-hand** and **right-hand** sides of the lane, allowing downstream consumers to correlate the centerline stationing with lane boundary discretization. (This table itself focuses on the station points and their progression.)

### Columns and meaning
1. **STATION**  
   Identifies the station index or station position along the lane reference path. It serves as the primary key for ordering the lane discretization and for linking to other lane-related datasets (e.g., neighbor nodes, influence calculations, or load distribution mapping).

2. **COORDINATES X, Y, Z**  
   Provides the 3D coordinates of the lane point at the given station. These coordinates are essential for reconstructing the geometry in global space and for any spatially dependent evaluation (e.g., projecting forces, computing distances, or visualizing the lane alignment).  
   - **X, Y** typically represent planar location.  
   - **Z** represents elevation.

3. **SECTION LENGTH**  
   Indicates the **distance from the current station to the next station** along the lane. This enables interpretation of the sampling resolution, calculation of segment lengths, and numerical integration or interpolation tasks that may depend on spacing.

4. **REMARKS**  
   Contains supplementary or descriptive data related to the geometry at that station. Specifically, it holds “data for geometry, radius, clothoidal etc.” This suggests that the lane alignment may be composed of varying curve primitives (e.g., circular arcs with **radius** and transition curves with **clothoids**). Remarks likely specify which geometric element is active at the station and the relevant parameters for that element.

### Data granularity
The table represents a **discretized longitudinal line** of the lane with associated geometric parameters captured at each station. It is therefore suitable for both visualization and for feeding geometry-aware computations (such as mapping influence regions or load distribution patterns to specific station positions).

The geometry of the lanes can be controlled with ECHO LINE. The default output results in a table for each lane with the following information in its headline:
 DY Influence width of the lane, see record LSEL DZ Influence height of the lane, see record LSEL Load distribution, see record LSEL
 The table contains the following columns:
 Data for geometry, radius, clothoidal etc.
 With ECHO LINE FULL one obtains a list of the neighbouring nodes at the left-hand side and to the right-hand side of the lane.

Influence lines can be represented and printed graphically. However, an output occurs only, if the lines have been selected with SHOW, and ECHO IL has not been set equal to NO. The graphical output is obtained only by using the record SIZE, whilst the output in the form of tables is obtained with ECHO IL FULL.
 The table of the influence lines contains in its headline the application point of the unit load and the scalar variable. The columns are as follows:
 X-VALUE X coordinate measured at the lane axis, beginning with 0.000 m PV-VALUE Influence line value for vertical loading verse wheel loadings MS-VALUE Influence line value for torsional loading PS-VALUE Influence line value for longitudinal loading (brake load) PQ-VALUE Influence line value for lateral loading

 (wind, centrifugal force) dPV/ds First derivative of the influence line values PV (corresponds to IL for -M loading) p+,p- for INT>2 r+,r- residual areas for INT>2
 Integrals of positive and negative influence values
 Integrals of influence values in the right and left
 Influence lines are plotted with a predetermined scale in the longitudinal direction and with a scale for the influence line values, which is determined by the height of the drawing bands. Maximum and minimum values are printed at the plot.
 For the graphics of the transverse influence line, the sum of the influence values of the the two wheels of the axle (Pv) and the integrals of the positive (p+) and negative (p-) influence values are also given. The values r+ and r- are the integrals of the residual areas outside the traffic lane.

This table is part of a structural “load trains” reporting system that prints the computed load definition for bridge/track-like loading schemes. Its output can be controlled: by default the generated loadings table can be suppressed with **ECHO TYPL NO**; it is expanded and the generated loadings are shown with **ECHO TYPL FULL**; and it is printed for user-defined loadings when **ECHO TYPL YES** is selected. The table is therefore primarily an explanatory/diagnostic listing of the load train elements and their governing parameters.

### Main columns and meaning
The table contains a set of columns describing each load segment and its type:

- **TYPE**: identifies the load element type. The table includes at least:
  - **Point load**
  - **E-0 Point load without dynamic factor**
  - **Distributed load with variable value**
- **E**: encodes the load formulation variant for point loading, specifically indicating whether a dynamic factor is applied.  
  - For **E-0**, the point load is explicitly stated to be **without the dynamic factor**.
  - For other point load cases, the dynamic treatment is handled elsewhere (in the dynamic factor/lane width table).
- **HF**: “Height of the gravity centre for centrifugal forces”. This is relevant for load cases where lateral/centrifugal effects require an elevation of the gravity centre to be considered. It appears as a parameter only for those load types where centrifugal effects are relevant.
- **LDEL** (implied output behavior): for loads with **variable length**, the output may include a **second line** showing:
  - the **maximum length**
  - the **minimum length**
  - and a possible **subdivision length** value  
  This information is placed in the **LDEL** column when such subdivision is applicable.

### Dynamic factors and lane width sub-table
In addition to the main load-definition table, the system outputs a separate table containing **dynamic factors** and **lane boundary positions**. These parameters define how loads act along stations (positions) and how lane placement and dynamic amplification are modeled.

Key fields in the supplementary dynamic/lane table are:
- **STARTING**: first station value (starting coordinate/position of the segment).
- **ENDING**: second station value (ending coordinate/position).
- **PHI1**: dynamic factor for **unfavourable bending**.
- **PHI2**: dynamic factor for **favourable bending**.
- **PHIS**: dynamic factor for **unfavourable shear**.
- **PHI4**: dynamic factor for **favourable shear**.
- **LPH**: determinant length (length over which the dynamic effects/determinant calculation is applied).
- **YRA**: lane boundary to the **right** of the first station.
- **YLA**: lane boundary to the **left** of the first station.
- **YRE**: lane boundary to the **right** of the second station.
- **YLE**: lane boundary to the **left** of the second station.

### Practical interpretation for RAG
Overall, this table should be indexed as a “load train element descriptor” where each row defines **what kind of load** (point, point without dynamic factor, or distributed variable), and related geometry/effect parameters (e.g., **HF** for centrifugal effects). When variable lengths exist, it additionally provides **min/max/subdivision** via **LDEL**. The dynamic behavior and lane positioning are captured in the associated supplementary parameters (**STARTING/ENDING**, **PHI*** factors, **LPH**, and **Y*** lane boundaries).

The load trains are described in plain text with their parameters. The output of the corre- sponding table can be suppressed with ECHO TYPL NO; with ECHO TYPL FULL the table is expanded in order to show the generated loadings. This table is also printed for user defined loadings by entering ECHO TYPL YES.

A table of the superposition combinations always appears when such combinations have been defined. A single line is printed for each combination containing its type as well as the partici- pated evaluation cases with their factors.

The evaluation results are controlled by the two ECHO options EVAL and RES.
 When one of these two options is active, a line which contains the identification of the position is printed for each position with corresponding influence lines.
 As long as EVAL is active, the position of the load train as well as the possible convoy distances or the variable lengths are output in a succeeding table.
 If EVAL is set to FULL, the regions with different signs are printed then for each evaluation case and for each lane together with the applied dynamic factors PHI1/PHI2 for unfavourably/- favourably acting loading and the positions of extreme values.
 If RES is active, the extreme values of the internal forces or other parameters are output in an additional table. The first columns contain the number, with which the load case has to be stored, and a text for the designation the evaluation rule.

If the ECHO option STAT is used, one receives an output which shows the used CPU time and the up to now needed memory allocation at the screen or in the logfile for each part of the program. These values are important, in order to allow an estimation of the memory and the CPU time requirements for larger examples.
